items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018
items.q: Van was very shy, but we did all this stuff in like two days... And he had this big bag of vegetable leaf... he would hardly come out of the booth... but you know he just brought these tunes out and we just played them.

ctx.x: What shape was the music in? Was it chord charts? Do you know?

Well see a lot of the things were just lead sheets with the chord changes on them. Occasionally there were certain things that were arranged. If he had an arranger there were certain lines we’d have to play. I was usually playing percussion. Because I didn’t have a reputation at all then as a drummer. And I wasn’t a very good drummer, because I had been trained as a percussionist. I mean I could play drums, but not to compete with the people who were playing in New York. You know, so I got a chance, even that was…
I just have this picture of you telling your grandkids, “You hear that song? I’m playing on that.” “Sure, Grandpa.”
